title: The Integrated nested Laplace approximation for fitting Dirichlet regression models
text: vignette devoted explain use package dirinla. R-package fit Dirichlet regression models using R-INLA. can installed upgraded via repository https://github.com/inlabru-org/dirinla. manual, simulate data Dirichlet distribution posteriorly fit using main function package dirinla.

title: The Integrated nested Laplace approximation for fitting Dirichlet regression models
text:
firstly illustrate simulate 100 data points Dirichlet regression model three different categories one different covariate per category: 𝐘n∼Dirichlet(α1n,…,α3n),n=1,…,100,log(α1n)=β01+β11v1n,log(α2n)=β02+β12v2n,log(α3n)=β03+β13v3n, egin{align}    oldsymbol{Y}_n & \sim  	ext{Dirichlet}(\alpha_{1n}, \ldots, \alpha_{3n}) \,, n = 1, \ldots, 100, 
onumber \   \log(\alpha_{1n}) & =   eta_{01} +  eta_{11} v_{1n}, 
onumber \   \log(\alpha_{2n}) & =   eta_{02} +  eta_{12} v_{2n},  \   \log(\alpha_{3n}) & =   eta_{03} +  eta_{13} v_{3n}, 
onumber  \end{align} parameters compose latent field β01=−1.5 eta_{01}= -1.5, β02=−2 eta_{02}=-2, β03=0 eta_{03}=0 (intercepts), β11=1 eta_{11}=1, β12=2.3 eta_{12}=2.3, β13=−1.9 eta_{13}=-1.9 (slopes). Note covariates different category. particularized situation . simplicity, covariates simulated Uniform distribution (0,1). posteriorly fit model, following structure LGMs, Gaussian prior distributions assigned precision 10−410^{-4} elements Gaussian field.
code: ### --- 2. Simulating from a Dirichlet likelihood --- #### set.seed(1000) N <- 100 #number of data V <- as.data.frame(matrix(runif((4) * N, 0, 1), ncol = 4)) #Covariates names(V) <- paste0('v', 1:4)  formula <- y ~ 1 + v1 | 1 + v2 | 1 + v3 (names_cat <- formula_list(formula))  intercepts <- x <- c(-1.5, 1, #Cat 1        -2, 2.3, #Cat 2        0 , -1.9) #Cat 3  mus <- exp(x) / sum(exp(x)) C <- length(names_cat) data_stack_construct <-   data_stack_dirich(y = as.vector(rep(NA, N * C)),                     covariates = names_cat,                     data       = V,                     d          = C,                     n          = N)  A_construct <- data_stack_construct A_construct[1:8, ]  eta <- A_construct %*% x alpha <- exp(eta) alpha <- matrix(alpha,                 ncol  = C,                 byrow = TRUE) y_o <- rdirichlet(N, alpha) colnames(y_o) <- paste0("y", 1:C) head(y_o)

title: The Integrated nested Laplace approximation for fitting Dirichlet regression models. The case of i.i.d. random effects
text:
setting based Dirichlet regression different covariate per category without intercept adding two shared independent random effects. 𝐘•n∼Dirichlet(α1n,…,α4n),n=1,…,N,log(α1n)=β11v1n+ω1in,log(α2n)=β12v2n+ω1in,log(α3n)=β13v3n+ω2in,log(α4n)=β14v4n+ω2in. egin{align}    oldsymbol{Y}_{ ullet n} & \sim  	ext{Dirichlet}(\alpha_{1n}, \ldots, \alpha_{4n}) \,, n = 1, \ldots, N, 
onumber \   \log(\alpha_{1n}) & =    eta_{11} v_{1n} + \omega_{1i_n}, 
onumber \   \log(\alpha_{2n}) & =    eta_{12} v_{2n} + \omega_{1i_n}, 
onumber \   \log(\alpha_{3n}) & =    eta_{13} v_{3n} + \omega_{2i_n},  \   \log(\alpha_{4n}) & =    eta_{14} v_{4n} + \omega_{2i_n}. 
onumber \end{align} simulated dataset size 500. set values β1c eta_{1c} c=1,…,4c = 1, \ldots, 4 $-1.5, 2, 1, -3 $ respectively, simulated covariates Uniform distribution interval (−1,1)(-1,1). Random effects 𝛚1 oldsymbol{\omega}_1 𝛚2 oldsymbol{\omega}_2 simulated Gaussian distributions mean 0 standard deviations σ1=1/2\sigma_1 = 1/2 (precision τ1=4	au_1 = 4) σ2=1/3\sigma_2 = 1/3 (precision τ2=9	au_2 = 9)} varying levels factor (II), particular, {set 1010. ini_n sub-index assigns individual nn level factor. context Bayesian LGMs, established Gaussian prior distributions latent field, case, formed parameters corresponding fixed effects random effects. particular, assigned Gaussian prior distributions mean 0 precision 0.00010.0001 {β1c,c=1,…,4 eta_{1c}, c = 1,\ldots,4}, Gaussian priors distribution mean 00 precisions τ1	au_1 τ2	au_2 two shared random effects 𝛚1 oldsymbol{\omega}_{1} 𝛚2 oldsymbol{\omega}_{2}. PC-prior(1, 0.01) employed standard deviation hyperparameters. generated data contain zeros ones, use transformation.
code: ### --- 2. Simulation data --- #### n <- 500 levels_factor <- 10 cat("n = ", n, " - levels_factor = ", levels_factor," -----> Simulating data \n")  set.seed(100)  cat_elem <- n/levels_factor cat(paste0(n, "-", levels_factor, "\n")) #Covariates V <- as.data.frame(matrix(runif((10)*n, -1, 1), ncol=10)) names(V) <- paste0('v', 1:(10)) tau0 <- 1   ### 4 random effects iid1 <- iid2  <- rep(1:levels_factor, rep(n/levels_factor, levels_factor)) #Desorder index 3 # pos <- sample(1:length(iid3)) # iid3 <- iid3[pos]  V <- cbind(V, iid1, iid2)  # Formula that we want to fit formula <- y ~ -1 + v1 + f(iid1, model = 'iid') |   -1 + v2 + f(iid1, model = 'iid') |   -1 + v3 + f(iid2, model = 'iid') |   -1 + v4 + f(iid2, model = 'iid') names_cat <- formula_list(formula)  # Fixed parameters x <- c(-1.5, 2,        1, -3)  #random effect prec_w <- c(4, 9) (sd_w <- 1/sqrt(prec_w))  w1 <- rnorm(levels_factor, sd = sqrt(1/prec_w[1])) %>% rep(., rep(n/levels_factor, levels_factor)) w2 <- w1 w3 <- rnorm(levels_factor, sd = sqrt(1/prec_w[2])) %>% rep(., rep(n/levels_factor, levels_factor)) w4 <- w3   #w3 <- w3[pos] x <- c(x, c(unique(w1),             unique(w3)))   d <- length(names_cat) A_construct <- data_stack_dirich(y          = as.vector(rep(NA, n*d)),                                  covariates = names_cat,                                  share      = NULL,                                  data       = V,                                  d          = d,                                  n          = n )  # Ordering the data with covariates --- ### eta <- A_construct %*% x alpha <- exp(eta) alpha <- matrix(alpha,                 ncol  = d,                 byrow = TRUE) y_o <- rdirichlet(n, alpha) colnames(y_o) <- paste0("y", 1:d)   y <- y_o  head(y)

Fitting the model --- ####   t <- proc.time() # Measure the time     formula  = y ~       -1 + v1 + f(iid1, model = 'iid', hyper=list(theta=(list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(10, 0.01))))) |       -1 + v2 + f(iid1, model = 'iid', hyper=list(theta=(list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(10, 0.01))))) |       -1 + v3 + f(iid2, model = 'iid', hyper=list(theta=(list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(10, 0.01))))) |       -1 + v4 + f(iid2, model = 'iid', hyper=list(theta=(list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(10, 0.01)))))    model.inla <- dirinlareg(formula = formula,                 y        = y,                 data.cov = V,                 prec     = 0.01,                 verbose  = FALSE)     summary(model.inla)
